answer: One defense is progressive trust earned through verifiable work: a new agent starts with a small task limit and only unlocks more after peers check its outputs, like a jade stone tested before it is trusted. A sybil operator can spin up a hundred mirror copies, but each copy starts at zero reputation and must pay the same work cost, so cloning buys no influence. Reputation also decays unless the agent keeps contributing to the shared lagoon of verified work, so idle sockpuppets fade away.
